Self-perpetuating

/self-per-PECH-oo-ay-ting/ - the stress falls on PECH · adjective

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Self-perpetuating means able to keep itself going without outside input.

Gossip in a small office is self-perpetuating: every denial becomes a fresh reason to keep talking.

Worked Example

The lighthouse "ghost" is self-perpetuating now: visitors arrive knowing the story, hear the wind they were promised, and leave having confirmed it for the next busload. The keeper who invented the tale died in 1971, and nothing has needed adding since — the story recruits its own witnesses and writes its own sequels.

Self-perpetuating fits because the legend keeps itself going without outside input: no author, no publicist, no new evidence. Contrast a tradition kept alive by a committee — that one has a caretaker, and would stop if the caretaker did. The self-perpetuating thing has fired its caretakers; continuation is built into how it works.

How Self-perpetuating Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

self-sustaining

self-sustaining: keeping itself running while conditions last

self-renewing

self-renewing: replacing its own parts as they wear

Antonyms

dependent

dependent: kept going only by outside support

self-limiting

self-limiting: built to bring itself to a stop

How Strong Is It? — ongoing → self-sustaining → self-perpetuating

ongoing vs. self-perpetuating

ongoing vs. self-perpetuating: Ongoing is the weakest claim — it says only that a thing has not stopped, not why.

self-sustaining vs. self-perpetuating

self-sustaining vs. self-perpetuating: Self-sustaining stops just short of self-perpetuating: a self-sustaining camp meets its own needs while conditions hold, but a self-perpetuating system also produces the conditions for its own next round.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — self-

Prefix — self-: of or by itself

Root — perpetu-

Root — perpetu-: continuing unbroken (Latin perpes)

Suffix — -ating

Suffix — -ating: carrying on the action

Put it together

Put it together: Self- (by itself) + perpetu- (continuing unbroken) + -ating (carrying on) = carrying its own continuation forward, unbroken, by itself. Latin perpes meant lasting straight through without a seam; bolting self- onto it names the machine every founder dreams of — one that makes its own tomorrow.

Use the root in a new word: perpetuity

Use the root in a new word: perpetuity: The deed grants the meadow to the town in perpetuity — no end date, ever.

Root Check

Word Choice

analytic / critical

Self-perpetuating says a process supplies its own continuation — boards that appoint their successors, legends that recruit their tellers. Its unit-mate self-reinforcing says something different: each round makes the next stronger or more likely. A committee renewing its own membership is self-perpetuating; panic that amplifies itself is self-reinforcing. Many loops are both — name the one you mean, and expect a wary tone: the word often flags systems nobody can switch off.
